paper_metadata.title: Coarse-to-fine Knowledge Graph Domain Adaptation based on Distantly-supervised Iterative Training
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper proposes an integrated framework for adapting and re-learning a knowledge graph from a general biomedical domain to a fine-grained oncology domain. It uses distant supervision and iterative training to discover domain-specific named entities and triplets from unlabeled text without manual annotation, with the goal of efficient oncology knowledge-graph construction.

problem_addressed: The paper addresses construction of a domain-specific oncology knowledge graph from large collections of raw or unlabeled biomedical text when manually annotated training data are scarce. It specifically adapts a coarse biomedical KG to oncology while recovering oncology-specific entities and relation triples absent from the source KG.

methodology.description: KGDA takes an existing coarse-domain KG K_c and an unlabeled target-domain corpus D, divides D into non-overlapping subsets, and alternates prediction, distant-corpus construction, and retraining. For the first subset, entity mentions are string-matched against K_c to create BIO-labelled NER data; relation instances are created from matched entity pairs, with NULL negatives sampled from unrelated pairs or out-of-domain words. Separate pretrained-language-model NER and RE classifiers are fine-tuned with cross-entropy. For later subsets, the current models predict entities and triples disjoint from K_c; high-confidence predictions are selected using probability and cumulative-frequency thresholds, added to the external knowledge bases, and used to create cumulative distant-supervision corpora for the next iteration. The final fine-domain KG combines overlapping triples with high-confidence target-domain triples. The method covers preprocessing, NER, entity typing through the source schema, relation/triple extraction, confidence filtering, and graph construction; separate coreference, entity linking, ontology discovery, and graph-validation modules are not reported.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The coarse biomedical KG defines the entity-type and relation-type inventory used for distant supervision and retained in the fine-domain KG: 18 entity types and 19 relation types. No external clinical ontology is used in the reported method; clinical ontology integration is identified as future work.

evaluation.setting: Biomedical-to-oncology adaptation using 240,000 unlabeled paragraphs. D1-D5 are used for iterative training and KG construction; D6 is held out. Held-out labels come from coarse-KG distant supervision, so this evaluates recovery of source-KG knowledge rather than recall of newly discovered oncology knowledge. Manual evaluation samples 50 cases each from high-confidence new entities, new-relation triples, and new-entity triples; one physician labels correctness, while recall cannot be estimated because the number of true fine-domain instances is unknown.
